name: Sonoma diet

lead: The Sonoma diet is a weight-management plan created by dietitian Connie Guttersen and introduced in January 2006 with her book. It is modelled on Mediterranean eating and combines portion control with ten 'power foods' such as almonds, blueberries, spinach and olive oil [1].

Its appearance payoff is fat loss and a trimmer waist, with attention to eating enjoyably. The book title promised a trimmer waist in ten days [1]. It has not been the subject of significant scholarly research [1].

paras: The plan runs in three waves: a 10-day first wave that restricts sugar and processed flour, a longer second wave that continues weight loss with more varied meals and permits wine, and a lifelong maintenance wave. Portions are guided by 7-inch plates and 2-cup bowls [1].

Critics cited in reference sources note that the first wave is restrictive, that no exercise advice is included, that it can cost more and take more cooking time, and that restricted eating can make vitamin and mineral intake harder to cover [1].

chain: Eat smaller portions of Mediterranean-style foods
Calorie intake falls and weight comes down
angle.text: The plan uses plate-size portion control and nutrient-dense foods to reduce calorie intake, aiming for fat loss and a trimmer midsection.

lead: The Sonoma diet is a lifestyle eating plan devised by nutritionist Connie Guttersen and derived from the Mediterranean diet [1]. It was introduced in January 2006 with her book The Sonoma Diet [2].

For looks, it is a fat-loss approach: reducing portion sizes and prioritising ten power foods (almonds, bell peppers, blueberries, broccoli, grapes, olive oil, spinach, strawberries, tomatoes and whole grains) to reach a leaner physique and smaller waist [2]. Proponents describe it as emphasising enjoyment of food rather than deprivation [2].
Encyclopedia sources note that it has not been the subject of significant scholarly research [2].

paras: Wave 1 lasts 10 days and targets eating habits tied to weight gain by restricting sugar and processed flour. Wave 2 is the main phase, with slower loss and more varied recipes, and moderate wine allowed. Wave 3 is maintenance, allowing occasional desserts, snacks and wine [2].
Portion control uses a plate-and-bowl system with 7-inch plates and 2-cup bowls [2].

Reference sources describe claims that the power foods are low in calorie and high in nutrients and that weight loss may lower risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease [2]. Criticisms noted include limited scholarly research, unproven benefits of wine, higher cost and cooking time, the absence of exercise recommendations, and possible difficulty meeting vitamin and mineral needs [2].

timeline.event: Connie Guttersen introduces the Sonoma diet with her book. [2]
